title: Lie groups, Part II: minimal parabolic subgroups, the Bruhat decomposition and the self-adjoint matrix model of real reductive groups
summary: Continue LieGroups Layer 9 retaining its full finite central matrix-cover Cartan datum and adding a compatible invariant form. Prove conjugacy of underlying involutions and Iwasawa choices with equal split centres, without identifying forms or auxiliary models. Compare N_K(𝔞)/Z_K(𝔞) with W(Σ) and characterize the component condition. Build P = MAN and its Langlands decomposition for every reductive Cartan datum, finite covers and disconnected groups included, and package it as RealSemisimpleLieGroups' minimal parabolic datum, whose Tits system, standard and general parabolics, Langlands decompositions, dynamical description and algebraic comparison are consumed. Beyond the component condition prove the Bruhat decomposition over N_K(𝔞)/Z_K(𝔞), ⁰L with component action on the split centre, the regular dynamical description, and the complexification criterion with centre. Adapt the supplied polar theorem to the intrinsic matrix tangent algebra, state the matrix headlines, and place real points of connected reductive ℝ-groups in the model.

layers.title: Reductive Cartan data and their conjugacy

targets.name: ReductiveCartanDatum
targets.statement: A reductive Cartan datum is a full LieGroups CartanInvolution I G, including global_model : FiniteCartanMatrixModel G θ, together with a symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form B on 𝔤, invariant under Ad(G) and dθ, with 𝔨 ⊥ 𝔭, negative on 𝔨 and positive on 𝔭. Retain the finite central covering onto a closed transpose-stable finite-component matrix subgroup, compatibility with transpose-inverse and pointwise fixation of the compact preimage. Consume the base polar diffeomorphism; do not add it as a field or a new theorem.
hypotheses: G is a real finite-dimensional C^infinity Lie group (LieGroup I ∞ G, FiniteDimensional ℝ E, T2Space G, BoundarylessManifold I G), 𝔤 = LeftInvariantDerivation I G

This compares involutions, not invariant forms or independently chosen matrix models; for semisimple 𝔤 the involutions are always conjugate (RealSemisimpleLieGroups 5.4 proves that case through maximal compact subgroups). The semisimple Lie-algebra step is RealSemisimpleLieGroups 0.2 applied to [𝔤,𝔤].

targets.name: zeroPart
targets.statement: For a reductive Cartan group L define ⁰L as the joint kernel of all continuous χ:L→ℝ_{>0}, V=𝔷(𝔩)∩𝔭_L, F=V^{Ad(L)}, V₀=F^⊥∩V for Bθ, and A_L=lieExp V. The component action on V is finite and orthogonal; its average is pr_F. The homomorphism h:L→F sends k exp X to the projection of X's split-central part, and positive characters are exactly exp∘ℓ∘h, ℓ∈F*. Thus ⁰L is closed normal, Lie(⁰L)=[𝔩,𝔩]⊕(𝔷∩𝔨_L)⊕V₀, ⁰L=K_L exp((𝔭_L∩[𝔩,𝔩])⊕V₀), the datum restricts to it, and multiplication ⁰L×exp(F)→L is a Lie-group isomorphism. When the component action on V is trivial (in particular under the component condition), F=V and V₀=0, giving ⁰L×A_L≅L. ⁰L is intrinsic; A_L and exp(F) depend on the datum. RealSemisimpleLieGroups 4.3 is the case L = L_{Π'} under the component condition (components fix the split centre 𝔞_{Π'}, and M_{Π'} = ⁰L_{Π'}); here components may move the split centre.
